title: Agririgo | Africa's Agricultural Intelligence Operating System
excerpt: A living digital twin of the farm, and fine-tuned AI that tells farmers where to act. Every field, pump and sensor is an object with state and history. Built for commercial farms in Zambia and South Africa.
content_html:
The intelligence layer for African agriculture

Your farm already has
the data. Now it can think.

Agririgo builds a living digital twin of your farm, where every field, tunnel, pump, solar array and sensor is an object with state and history. Rigo AI reads that twin and tells you where to act, ranked, with the reason it is saying so. Built for commercial farms in Zambia and South Africa.

No account needed. Your images stay on your device.

What Agririgo is

A living digital twin of the farm.

Agririgo connects every source a farm already has into one structure, where the things on the farm are objects with state and history. Rigo AI reads that structure and returns ranked actions, running on the farm's own machine, with consent.

  • Farm softwarekeeps records
  • Drone toolsmake maps
  • Generic AIanswers, then forgets

Agririgo connects them, and remembers every field.

One ontology, models fine-tuned on African conditions, and engineers who come to the farm and map the operation before anything is built.

How a deployment works

Inside the twin

Everything on the farm, held as an object.

Tunnels, pivots, solar, herds and drones stop being separate systems. Each has a state today and a history behind it, and Rigo AI reads them together.

Readings shown are illustrative

Market access, not just transparency

Two regulations now decide whether your crop can be sold abroad.

Traceability stopped being a goodwill exercise. For a growing list of crops, an importer in the EU or the US cannot legally accept your consignment without records you are expected to produce on demand. RigoTrace is built to hold exactly those records, per lot, from the day you plant.

EU Deforestation Regulation

EUDR · Regulation (EU) 2023/1115

Applies to coffee, cocoa, soy, palm oil, cattle, rubber and timber entering the EU. Operators must hold plot-level geolocation for the land the commodity was grown on, plus a due-diligence statement proving it was not linked to deforestation.

What RigoTrace holds: field and plot identification per lot, chain of custody through aggregation, and an exportable record for your due-diligence filing.

US FDA Food Traceability Rule

FSMA Section 204

Applies to foods on the FDA Food Traceability List, including many fresh fruits and vegetables. Anyone in the chain must keep Key Data Elements at each Critical Tracking Event and produce them to the FDA within 24 hours of a request.

What RigoTrace holds: harvest, packing, and shipping events with lot codes and dates, exportable as a sortable spreadsheet.

How EUDR works for producers →

Compliance dates for both regimes have been amended more than once and differ by company size. Confirm the deadline that applies to you with your importer or the official register before you plan around it. Agririgo holds the records; it does not file on your behalf and is not a substitute for legal advice.

Proof, not a promise

Scan this with your phone, right now.

This is not a picture of a QR code. It is a live one, pointing at a real passport in our production system. You do not need an account, an app, or our permission to check it.

No signal? The same code resolves at verify.agririgo.com, a separate deployment that stays up independently of this site.

On African farms

Precision agriculture that fits how the work is actually done here.

A drone where there is one, a phone where there is not, and a person walking the rows either way. Nothing here assumes a connected tractor or a permanent internet connection.

The problem

The data exists.
The decision comes too late.

Farms run on data that never talks to itself. Soil sensors, pumps, solar, drones, IoT, satellite, spreadsheets and WhatsApp, each in its own silo. Commercial farms hold the most data of anyone in agriculture, and still decide by walking the land.

In 2023/24 drought destroyed 982,765 hectares of Zambian maize and affected more than 9 million people across 84 of 117 districts. The data existed. The decision came too late.

Agririgo is built for the whole continent. Our open data runs deepest in Zambia, where the national statistics are strongest, and the platform itself is not country-specific: the models, the languages and the offline paths work wherever the field is.

Rigo Studio

One photograph. Real hectares. A record your buyer can check.

Rigo Studio reads the altitude your drone already wrote into the file, so a traced weed patch comes back as square metres and a count becomes plants per hectare. Rigo AI names what it sees, your corrections train a detector your aircraft can carry, and the finding follows the crop all the way to the QR code on the bag.

It runs on your device. Nothing uploads, nothing queues, and there is no flight to plan first.

Drone pilots and service providers

You can already fly. This is the part clients actually pay for.

  • Real areas from one photo, using the altitude DJI writes into every JPEG
  • Stand density per hectare without stitching an orthomosaic
  • A client report instead of a folder of JPEGs
  • Export a training set so your drone learns to spot it in flight

Agronomists and co-op officers

Evidence you can put in front of a member or a buyer.

  • Trace regions to get hectares affected, not a vague impression
  • Every finding carries the evidence that produced it, so you can disagree
  • Findings and areas export as data, not a screenshot

Researchers and students

A labelling workstation that costs nothing and locks nothing in.

  • COCO export with segmentation, readable by every training toolchain
  • The vegetation index runs on your device, so no upload and no queue
  • Publish to the community repository so others can build on it

Exporters and processors

Connect what you saw in the field to what you ship.

  • Attach field evidence to the Crop Passport a buyer scans
  • Per-farmer attribution survives into pooled lots
  • Weak claims stay visibly weak rather than being dressed up

A different question

Survey platforms answer what does my whole farm look like, and that needs a planned flight, an hour of processing and a subscription. Studio answers what is wrong in front of me, how much of it there is, and can I prove it to my buyer. Different job, different tool.

content_html_zh:
The intelligence layer for African agriculture

Your farm already hasthe data. Now it can think.

Agririgo builds a living digital twin of your farm, where every field, tunnel, pump, solar array and sensor is an object with state and history. Rigo AI reads that twin and tells you where to act, ranked, with the reason it is saying so. Built for commercial farms in Zambia and South Africa.

无需帐户。 Your images stay on your device.

What Agririgo is

A living digital twin of the farm.

Agririgo connects every source a farm already has into one structure, where the things on the farm are objects with state and history. Rigo AI reads that structure and returns ranked actions, running on the farm's own machine, with consent.

  • Farm softwarekeeps records
  • Drone toolsmake maps
  • Generic AIanswers, then forgets

Agririgo connects them, and remembers every field.

One ontology, models fine-tuned on African conditions, and engineers who come to the farm and map the operation before anything is built.

How a deployment works

Inside the twin

Everything on the farm, held as an object.

Tunnels, pivots, solar, herds and drones stop being separate systems. Each has a state today and a history behind it, and Rigo AI reads them together.

Readings shown are illustrative

Market access, not just transparency

Two regulations now decide whether your crop can be sold abroad.

Traceability stopped being a goodwill exercise. For a growing list of crops, an importer in the EU or the US cannot legally accept your consignment without records you are expected to produce on demand. RigoTrace is built to hold exactly those records, per lot, from the day you plant.

EU Deforestation Regulation

EUDR · Regulation (EU) 2023/1115

Applies to coffee, cocoa, soy, palm oil, cattle, rubber and timber entering the EU. Operators must hold plot-level geolocation for the land the commodity was grown on, plus a due-diligence statement proving it was not linked to deforestation.

What RigoTrace holds: field and plot identification per lot, chain of custody through aggregation, and an exportable record for your due-diligence filing.

US FDA Food Traceability Rule

FSMA Section 204

Applies to foods on the FDA Food Traceability List, including many fresh fruits and vegetables. Anyone in the chain must keep Key Data Elements at each Critical Tracking Event and produce them to the FDA within 24 hours of a request.

What RigoTrace holds: harvest, packing, and shipping events with lot codes and dates, exportable as a sortable spreadsheet.

How EUDR works for producers →

Compliance dates for both regimes have been amended more than once and differ by company size. Confirm the deadline that applies to you with your importer or the official register before you plan around it. Agririgo holds the records; it does not file on your behalf and is not a substitute for legal advice.

Proof, not a promise

Scan this with your phone, right now.

This is not a picture of a QR code. It is a live one, pointing at a real passport in our production system. You do not need an account, an app, or our permission to check it.

On African farms

Precision agriculture that fits how the work is actually done here.

A drone where there is one, a phone where there is not, and a person walking the rows either way. Nothing here assumes a connected tractor or a permanent internet connection.

The data exists.The decision comes too late.

Farms run on data that never talks to itself. Soil sensors, pumps, solar, drones, IoT, satellite, spreadsheets and WhatsApp, each in its own silo. Commercial farms hold the most data of anyone in agriculture, and still decide by walking the land.

In 2023/24 drought destroyed 982,765 hectares of Zambian maize and affected more than 9 million people across 84 of 117 districts. The data existed. The decision came too late.

Agririgo is built for the whole continent. Our open data runs deepest in Zambia, where the national statistics are strongest, and the platform itself is not country-specific: the models, the languages and the offline paths work wherever the field is.

Rigo Studio

One photograph. Real hectares. A record your buyer can check.

Rigo Studio reads the altitude your drone already wrote into the file, so a traced weed patch comes back as square metres and a count becomes plants per hectare. Rigo AI names what it sees, your corrections train a detector your aircraft can carry, and the finding follows the crop all the way to the QR code on the bag.

It runs on your device. Nothing uploads, nothing queues, and there is no flight to plan first.
